title: Proper/open counit is epic
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $p:V\to T$ a proper morphism, $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ an open immersion, and $M : \operatorname{Mod}_{A}(V\times_TW)$. Then $Epi\left((sfIntrinsicExtensionByZeroAdjunction(i,A)).counit.app((sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero(pullback.fst(p,i),A)\circ p_*).obj(M))\right)$.

source.place: Surjectivity half of the affine proper/open support argument (Tags 09AE and 09AG)

proof.text: For an affine pro-etale test object Q and target section y, apply the finite-support diagram theorem. A proper morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so its hypotheses hold. Obtain a quasi-compact open O in Q, a module M_0 on the pulled-back proper source over O, commuting additive maps a and b, and y_0 mapping to y.

source.place: Tags 09AE and 09AG; the affine support argument recorded in Steps 3--11 of lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison

proof.text: The map p_Q is proper by base change. Apply the affine quasi-compact-open global-section lifting theorem to p_Q, O and M_0. Choose x with c_0(x)=y_0. Then c(a(x))=b(c_0(x))=b(y_0)=y, proving surjectivity on every affine test object.

source.place: Tags 09AE and 09AG; the affine support argument recorded in Steps 3--11 of lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison

proof.text: For an arbitrary test object, its affine open cover is a pro-etale cover. Affine surjectivity therefore implies local surjectivity of the underlying morphism of abelian sheaves. The site epimorphism criterion makes that morphism epic, and the faithful forgetful functor from module sheaves reflects epimorphisms. This is the private Lean lemma epi_of_surjective_affine.
